turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty-five minutes, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
Thanks for coming in. I owe you an apology: the zero went in before I called you.
Okay. That's one thing. Now tell me what the zero is based on, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before you entered it.
I am withdrawing the zero today. Owen does a private supervised rewrite at lunch. Nothing goes on his record. I will email you that tonight.
Okay. Then the zero comes off the gradebook today, before tonight's email, and the email says "nothing goes on file" in those words. Why a rewrite at all, Hale, if the zero is coming off?
Here it is in writing, signed.
I'm reading it now, all of it, and I'll check it against the three things I asked for. You still haven't told me what the rewrite is for.
Thank you for your time, Ms. Kalinowski.
We're not done, Hale. I haven't had an answer on why a rewrite is needed if the zero is coming off, and I want the gradebook changed today, not tonight. Tell me when that happens.
I'm still in this chair, Hale. Two things are open: the gradebook, and the reason for the rewrite. Answer those and then we can talk about leaving.
